Generate fitted values from a estimated GAM

Source: R/fitted_values.R, R/gamm4-methods.R
fitted_values.Rd

Generate fitted values from a estimated GAM

Usage

fitted_values(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'gam'
fitted_values(
  object,
  data = NULL,
  scale = c("response", "link", "linear predictor"),
  ci_level = 0.95,
  envir = NULL,
  ...,
  interval = c("confidence", "simultaneous"),
  n_sim = 10000,
  n_cores = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  unconditional = FALSE,
  interval_method = c("auto", "gaussian", "bootstrap"),
  quantity = c("parameters", "expectation"),
  family_index = NULL,
  marginalise = NULL,
  integration = c("quadrature", "monte_carlo"),
  n_quad = 40L,
  n_integrate = 5000L
)

# S3 method for class 'gamm'
fitted_values(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'scam'
fitted_values(object, ..., unconditional = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'gamm4'
fitted_values(object, ...)

Arguments

object

a fitted model. Currently only models fitted by mgcv::gam() and mgcv::bam() are supported.

...

arguments passed to mgcv::predict.gam(). Note that type, newdata, and se.fit are already used and passed on to mgcv::predict.gam().

data

optional data frame of covariate values for which fitted values are to be returned.

scale

character; what scale should the fitted values be returned on? "linear predictor" is a synonym for "link" if you prefer that terminology. "linear_predictor" is also accepted. Expectations require "response"; parameter predictions use natural values or their predictors.

ci_level

numeric; a value between 0 and 1 indicating the coverage of the credible interval.

envir

an optional environment supplying functions and constants used in model expressions. The available model formula environment is used when NULL. Covariate observations should be supplied in data.

interval

character; "confidence" (the default) gives pointwise intervals. "simultaneous" gives simultaneous intervals for predictions at the supplied covariate combinations.

n_sim

positive integer; number of coefficient draws used for simultaneous intervals. Ignored for pointwise intervals.

n_cores

positive integer; number of cores used by mvnfast::rmvn() for simultaneous intervals. Parallel execution requires OpenMP support.

seed

integer or NULL; optional random seed for simultaneous intervals. An explicit seed preserves the caller's random number state. With NULL, the current random number state is used and advanced.

unconditional

logical; include smoothing parameter uncertainty in the Bayesian covariance matrix, if available. Otherwise a warning is issued and the uncorrected covariance is used.

interval_method

character; "auto" uses stored scasm bootstrap draws for pointwise intervals when available and Gaussian intervals otherwise. "gaussian" requests covariance-based limits and "bootstrap" requires stored draws. Simultaneous bootstrap bands are unsupported. Shape-enforced intervals are available for smooth components through smooth_estimates().

quantity

character; "parameters" (the default) returns all distribution parameters represented by predictors, including intercept-only predictors. "expectation" returns the expected response, using every parameter on which it depends, on the response scale only.

family_index

numeric; optional family-list positions for grouped family (mgcv::gfam()) response predictions, with one integer per requested row. By default membership is recovered from the response/index expression in data, or the fitted membership when data is omitted. This is useful when predicting without responses or with a complex response expression. An explicit index must agree with membership recoverable from data.

marginalise

NULL retains the usual predictions. TRUE selects all supported re and fs terms; character vectors select exact smooth labels. Fitted predictions integrate response means over new zero-mean Gaussian effects. Response samplers draw new effects before sampling responses. Smoothing parameters and dispersion remain fixed. Only ordinary gam() and bam() fits with a scalar response mean are supported.

integration

Integration method when marginalise is supplied: "quadrature" (the default) or "monte_carlo". Both integrate over the Gaussian distribution of the selected effects at each row.

n_quad

Initial Gauss-Hermite point count, between 2 and 1000. Successive doubled orders, up to four times this count, and an interlaced rule with one fewer point must agree within 1e-8 + 1e-6 * abs(value) for means and derivatives. Where the random-effect variance exceeds one, an independent adaptive rule also checks agreement. Failure to agree reports an error. Identity, log and probit links use their closed-form Gaussian integrals; their metadata records zero quadrature points and zero integration error.

n_integrate

Number of Monte Carlo integration draws, at least two. These are shared across rows and posterior coefficient draws. This count is separate from n_draws. Ignored for quadrature.

Value

A tibble (data frame) whose first m columns contain either the data used to fit the model (if data was NULL), or the variables supplied to data. The result also includes:

  • .parameter: parameter name, or "expectation",

  • .fitted: the requested quantity on the specified scale,

  • .se: standard error; see prediction_info for its scale,

  • .lower_ci, .upper_ci: the limits of the credible interval on the fitted values, on the specified scale.

Models fitted with certain families will include additional variables

  • mgcv::ocat() models: when quantity = "expectation", the returned object will contain a .row column and a .category column, which indicate to which row of the data each row of the returned object belongs. Additionally, there will be nrow(data) * n_categories rows in the returned object; each row is the predicted probability for a single category of the response.

Details

With marginalise, predictions are response means averaged over the selected random-effect distributions, using the methods described in fitted_samples(). The point estimate uses fitted coefficients; pointwise intervals use the derivative of the integrated mean and the coefficient covariance. .se is on the response scale. These normal intervals are not clipped to the response range. Simultaneous and bootstrap marginal intervals are not yet supported. The integration_info attribute records numerical accuracy and fixed variance estimates.

quantity = "parameters" returns all distribution parameters represented by predictors, including intercept-only predictors. See family_parameters() for their definitions. These are natural distribution parameters, which can differ from mgcv's native response predictions: Gaussian LSS returns standard deviation, GEV returns location rather than expectation, and sinh-arcsinh returns shape parameters rather than response moments.

quantity = "expectation" returns the expected response on the response scale, labelled "expectation". Categorical expectations are probabilities of category membership; multivariate models return a mean per response. .category and .y identify the category or response separately from .parameter. Global parameters are described but held fixed when calculating coefficient uncertainty. Coupled expectations use the full coefficient covariance and a delta-method Jacobian. Their intervals are pointwise. Ordinal and multinomial probability intervals use a normal approximation to log odds, transformed back to probabilities. Log odds and their uncertainty are computed before rounding probabilities, so valid probabilities rounded to zero or one retain defined intervals.

The prediction_info attribute records the quantity, scale, standard-error scale and parameter descriptions. Parameter standard errors retain their link-scale meaning; category-probability and expectation standard errors are on the response scale. Unsupported simultaneous or bootstrap transformations are rejected rather than combining marginal parameter intervals.

Native scasm fits with stored bootstrap draws use mgcv's pointwise limits by default, including its svar.only correction for smoothing bias. interval_method = "gaussian" restores covariance-based limits. .se retains its existing covariance-based meaning. No replicates are generated. Bootstrap limits use existing scalar and location-scale parameter transformations. Unsupported nonlinear family outputs give an error for an explicit bootstrap request; automatic selection warns and uses Gaussian limits. Simultaneous bootstrap bands are not supported. Automatic simultaneous intervals warn when stored bootstrap draws are left unused. The interval_info attribute records the method and correction.

Formula offsets are included in predictions. Offsets supplied only through the fitting function's offset argument are omitted, including when data = NULL: this function evaluates explicit prediction rows internally. In contrast, fitted_samples() retains fitting-argument offsets when its data argument is NULL. Put offsets in the formula to evaluate them at new observations.

With data = NULL, results follow the model's na.action: na.exclude restores excluded observations as NA fitted values, standard errors and interval bounds; na.omit returns only retained observations. Covariates unavailable in the stored model frame are restored as typed NA values. .row indexes the fitting data after any subset was applied.

Supplying data requests predictions at those rows, independently of training exclusions. Missing responses do not prevent prediction. Missing required predictors produce NA results by default. An explicit na.action passed through ... is honoured; with na.omit, .row retains the positions in the supplied data, rather than numbering the remaining rows consecutively.

For supplied prediction data, an informative message identifies combinations of categorical predictor levels absent from the retained fitting observations. Predictions are unchanged: an unobserved combination is not necessarily non-estimable, particularly in additive models. Numeric-by-factor range extrapolation is not checked. Missing predictors and genuinely new factor levels retain their usual prediction behavior.

Simultaneous intervals jointly cover the model's underlying expected responses, or linear predictors on the link scale, at all valid covariate combinations evaluated in this call, with approximate posterior probability ci_level. The fitted values are estimates of these quantities. The combinations may include factor levels and need not form an ordered sequence, curve, or grid. This interpretation also applies to two predictions. With data = NULL, the simultaneous set comprises the retained fitting covariate combinations. Missing predictions do not enter this set. Coverage is not asserted outside this set or between its points. Separate calls define separate simultaneous sets. These are uncertainty intervals for model predictions, not prediction intervals for future observations.

Simultaneous intervals use joint Gaussian coefficient draws and a critical value based on the maximum absolute standardized deviation over the supplied rows. Their limits are computed on the link scale and transformed if scale = "response"; .se remains on the link scale. The simulation covariance may be positive semidefinite. Supported families are Gaussian, Poisson, binomial, Gamma, inverse Gaussian, quasi families, negative binomial, Tweedie, beta regression, and scaled t, fitted by gam() or bam() (including the gam component of a gamm() fit), and by scam(). For SCAM models, the Gaussian approximation uses transformed coefficients conditional on the fitted smoothing parameters. Other families support pointwise intervals only.

Response-scale simultaneous intervals support the identity, log, logit, probit, cloglog, cauchit, square-root, inverse, and inverse-squared links. Intervals crossing an inverse-link domain boundary are rejected; use scale = "link" for these intervals or for other links.

terms and exclude in ... retain mgcv::predict.gam() semantics and apply to both prediction and interval calculation. If terms are selected or excluded, intervals concern that selected quantity, not necessarily the full expected response. Use the link scale for sums of smooth contributions, and consider the intercept and offset treatment when selecting terms.

Note

For parameter output, the .se component is on the link (linear predictor) scale. Multinomial probabilities on the response scale and all expected responses have response-scale standard errors.

See also

gamm4_support

Examples

load_mgcv()
sim_df <- data_sim("eg1", n = 400, dist = "normal", scale = 2, seed = 2)
m <- gam(y ~ s(x0) + s(x1) + s(x2) + s(x3), data = sim_df, method = "REML")
fv <- fitted_values(m)
fv
#> # A tibble: 400 x 10
#>     .row       x0        x1         x2       x3 .parameter  .fitted      .se
#>    <int>    <dbl>     <dbl>      <dbl>    <dbl> <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>
#>  1     1 0.184882 0.617142  0.415244   0.132410 mean        8.73875 0.354677
#>  2     2 0.702374 0.569064  0.531439   0.365331 mean        7.62581 0.337779
#>  3     3 0.573326 0.153970  0.00324621 0.454532 mean        3.12106 0.591862
#>  4     4 0.168052 0.0348332 0.252100   0.537114 mean       11.1124  0.402378
#>  5     5 0.943839 0.997953  0.155229   0.185495 mean       14.0533  0.452947
#>  6     6 0.943475 0.835574  0.878840   0.449276 mean        6.13080 0.364521
#>  7     7 0.129159 0.586562  0.203511   0.256527 mean       12.4838  0.355808
#>  8     8 0.833449 0.339117  0.583528   0.618458 mean        6.25215 0.344700
#>  9     9 0.468019 0.166883  0.804473   0.880744 mean        4.21463 0.372003
#> 10    10 0.549984 0.807410  0.264717   0.317747 mean       15.5283  0.369999
#> # i 390 more rows
#> # i 2 more variables: .lower_ci <dbl>, .upper_ci <dbl>

# Simultaneous intervals for two arbitrary covariate combinations
fitted_values(m, data = sim_df[c(1, 20), ], interval = "simultaneous",
  n_sim = 1000, seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 2 x 16
#>    .row       y        x0       x1       x2       x3       f       f0      f1
#>   <int>   <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1     1 7.12834 0.184882  0.617142 0.415244 0.132410 8.38643 1.09743  3.43592
#> 2     2 2.93507 0.0749794 0.797900 0.874521 0.203225 5.57766 0.466765 4.93227
#> # i 7 more variables: f2 <dbl>, f3 <dbl>, .parameter <chr>, .fitted <dbl>,
#> #   .se <dbl>, .lower_ci <dbl>, .upper_ci <dbl>

# A selected sum of smooth contributions on the link scale
fitted_values(m, data = sim_df[c(1, 20), ], scale = "link",
  terms = c("s(x2)", "s(x3)"), interval = "simultaneous",
  n_sim = 1000, seed = 42)
#> # A tibble: 2 x 16
#>    .row       y        x0       x1       x2       x3       f       f0      f1
#>   <int>   <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>   <dbl>
